_why: ADR 0144's mutation table, re-derived under scripts/mutate.py.
ADR 0144 is the one that fixed check_mutation_tables_reproducible.py so
it could see a table indented inside a bullet. It then published its own
mutation table -- and was immediately flagged by the rule it had just
restored to working order. That is the guard behaving correctly on its
own author, and it is the reason this file exists.
The mutations restore the two invented citations from the README: the
original `ref 12345`, which appeared in no fixture at all, and a
plausible-looking `ref 999999`. The subtler defect ADR 0144 also found --
`ref 649716`, a real ACETYLCHOLINESTERASE reference printed under a
lactate dehydrogenase example -- is deliberately NOT here, because the
guard does not catch it and the ADR says so. A set file that implied
test: cd Tests && python3 -m pytest test_documented_citations_guard.py --no-header -p no:cacheprovider

mutations.description: the guard stops checking whether a cited id exists
mutations._note: The whole check, removed. Everything still prints -- the counts, the OK line -- so a reader watching the output would see a guard that looks like it ran.

mutations.description: an empty fixture corpus passes vacuously instead of failing
mutations._note: With no reference ids loaded, every citation is trivially 'unknown' or trivially fine depending on which way the check leans. Failing loudly and naming the fixtures as the cause is the only honest option; passing would make the guard strongest exactly when it knows least.
mutations.find:
if not known:
        # An empty corpus would make every citation "unknown" and the check
mutations.replace:
if False:
        # An empty corpus would make every citation "unknown" and the check

mutations.description: a missing surface is skipped rather than reported
mutations._note: The failure mode check_non_affiliation_notice.py names explicitly: the easiest way to defeat a checklist is to delete the thing being checked, and a guard that shrugs at a missing file rewards exactly that.
